title: Loan default and credit score disputes - the legal remedies
p1:
A missed loan payment can hurt your credit score, but what if the report itself is wrong?

Many people assume that once a bank reports a default, they have no option left.
p2:
The surprising fact is that credit reports are not final judgments. If incorrect information, duplicate entries, or outdated records affect your score, you can challenge them.

A credit bureau must investigate disputes and correct inaccurate information after verification. A lender cannot simply keep reporting wrong details without accountability.
p3:
The practical step is to collect loan statements, payment proofs, and credit report records before raising a dispute. If the issue is not resolved, borrowers may explore further legal remedies through appropriate consumer and regulatory channels.

A damaged credit score can affect future loans, jobs, and financial opportunities, so checking your credit report regularly is a smart habit.
